If a thunderstorm catches you outside, do not shelter under a tree.
Lightning hits the tree, and part of the current jumps to you.
Do not lie flat on the ground. That only puts more of you in the path of the current running through it.
And crouching down does not make you any safer.
If you can hear thunder, the lightning is close enough to strike you.
So run for a real building, or a car with a metal roof and the windows up.
A tent, a porch or a picnic shelter will not protect you.
Nothing in reach? Get off the hill, get away from water, and stay clear of fences.
Then stay inside until thirty minutes after the last thunder.
And if someone is hit, you can touch them. They hold no charge. Call for help.
